rules.title: Writable folder in the system PATH
rules.subject: {dir}
rules.why: Services and other SYSTEM processes that try to load a DLL that doesn't exist fall back to the folders in the system PATH. A DLL planted in a writable PATH folder under the right name loads as SYSTEM.
rules.fix: Remove the folder from the system PATH if nothing needs it there, or remove write access for non-admin accounts. Tool installers that live in C:\<Tool> and add it to PATH are the usual cause; install them under Program Files instead.

rules.title: Missing system PATH folder can be created by non-admins
rules.subject: {dir}
rules.why: The folder doesn't exist, but non-admins can create it. Whoever creates it controls a folder in the system PATH, and can plant DLLs that SYSTEM processes will find there.
rules.fix: Remove the stale entry from the system PATH. If it's still needed, create the folder now with an ACL that only lets Administrators and SYSTEM write to it.
